messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 58-year-old male presents to his primary care physician complaining of a painless bump on his penis. He first noticed the lesion 1 year ago but was too embarrassed to mention the issue at his last annual physical exam. The lesion has since grown in size and has recently become more erythematous. He has hypertension treated with lisinopril. At age 45, he was successfully treated for phimosis with a steroid cream. He first engaged in sexual intercourse at age 14 and has had “too many sexual partners to count” in his lifetime. He smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years but quit 10 years ago. He drinks one alcoholic beverage daily. Physical examination shows a nontender 5 mm x 5 mm ulcerated lesion with an erythematous base on the dorsum of the glans. There is no inguinal lymphadenopathy. Excisional biopsy of the lesion is performed. Which of the following pathological findings is most likely to be seen on the biopsy specimen?

Options:
A. Atypical squamous cells with varying degrees of mitotic activity
B. Spirochetes on dark-field microscopy
C. Nonspecific inflammatory features with C. trachomatis amplification on PCR
D. Multinucleated giant cells on Tzanck smear
E. Safety pin-shaped intracellular inclusions that appear purple on Giemsa stain

Correct answer: A. Atypical squamous cells with varying degrees of mitotic activity

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This question tests pathology of penile squamous cell carcinoma; the patient's embarrassment is incidental and no psychiatric knowledge is tested."}
